purpose: Sotagliflozin is used to lower the risk of serious heart problems, such as hospitalization for heart failure or death from heart or blood vessel disease, in adults who have heart failure or type 2 diabetes with kidney disease and other heart risk factors. It helps protect your heart and keep fluid from building up in your body. It is not primarily used just to lower blood sugar, though it can help with that too.
how_it_works: This medicine works by blocking two proteins in your body called SGLT1 and SGLT2. These proteins normally help your body reabsorb sugar and sodium back into the blood. By blocking them, the medicine helps your kidneys flush out extra sugar and sodium through your urine, which takes pressure off your heart and reduces fluid buildup. Think of it as helping your kidneys act like a drain to remove things your body does not need.
common_side_effects: Low blood pressure or dizziness especially when standing up, increased urination, yeast infections in the genital area, urinary tract infections, diarrhea, and low blood sugar especially if you take other diabetes medications.
warnings: This medicine can cause a rare but serious condition called diabetic ketoacidosis, where acids build up in your blood even if your blood sugar is not very high — seek help right away if you feel nauseated, vomit, have stomach pain, or feel confused. It can also increase the risk of a serious genital infection called Fournier's gangrene. Do not use this medicine if your kidneys are on dialysis. Stay well hydrated and let your doctor know before any surgery or major illness so dosing can be adjusted safely.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 200 mg taken by mouth once daily, taken just before your first meal of the day. Your doctor may increase it to 400 mg once daily depending on how you tolerate it and how well your kidneys are working. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
